A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PAD, with readable main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Renamed components and reorganized supplementary sections can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original alignment experiments, GPT-4 judgments, decoding sensitivity results, and inference timings.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices C and F report original alignment results, resource measurements, and generated case-study outputs.

M1.justification: The reward decomposition, two-stage reward-model training, loss, and guided decoding procedure remain unchanged. Renaming PRM to PersRM and adding Algorithms 1–2 document the existing method rather than introduce new components.

E1.justification: Reported coverage contracts: Section 4.1.1 and Table A1 remove the UltraFeedback training component, including its instruction-following, truthfulness, and honesty annotations. The four additional 'friendly' preference evaluations in v5 Appendix B.2 also disappear. These materially narrow training and generalization coverage, although v6 retains an inconsistent UltraFeedback preprocessing reference.

E2.justification: Table 2 replaces ARGS with Aligner (Ji et al., 2024) on both datasets. Other comparator families remain; ARGS's retained related-work citation and checklist entry do not constitute a retained experimental comparison.

E3.justification: Table 2 introduces explicit single-dimension and joint three-dimension configurations, including additional conditions for Preference Prompting and MetaAligner. The documented training prompt changes to a user-side Guidelines/Principles/Instruction template, Figure 5 changes the reported beta sweep from 0–2.0 to 0–1.5, and memory becomes an evaluation metric. These are reported protocol changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix F.4 adds a controlled steering case comparing preferences for one fixed internship-offer instruction. Resource analysis expands to memory usage, and the beta sensitivity analysis is revised. The k sensitivity analysis and three earlier case comparisons remain.

E5.justification: Table C2 newly labels its summaries 'mean and variance,' while retaining the dispersion values and Section 4.3's description of standard deviations across three runs. This is a limited, inconsistent uncertainty-labeling change; no additional runs, seeds, or statistical tests are documented.

E6.justification: Core results are substantially revised. On P-Soups, v5 Table 2 reports PAD's overall reward/win rate as 1.06/84%; v6 reports 1.28/84% for single-dimension and 0.85/78% for joint alignment. These are revised configuration-specific results, not established same-setting gains. Figures 2 and 5 and Table 3 aggregates also change; memory measurements are added and the friendly-preference results are removed.

T1.justification: The definitions, derivations, generalization bound, and proof steps are retained, with proofs moving from Appendix C to D. Replacing optimal-policy superscripts with stars and clarifying preference indices do not change the mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: personalized reward decomposition, alignment without additional policy training, superiority over existing methods, and generalization across preferences and base models.

C2.justification: V6 adds a favorable interpretation of the memory/speed tradeoff and explains preference-dependent behavior in the new steering case. Section 4.4 removes the explanation linking weaker cross-model gains to mismatched MDP dynamics. The general limitations paragraph is retained in Appendix E.

D1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 and reference-model initialization/freezing details expand implementation documentation, and the abstract adds a model/code hyperlink. Conversely, Table 3 removes model-specific beta values and the ARGS reproduction instructions disappear. Existing LoRA, hardware, and training hyperparameters remain.

R1.justification: V6 adds the Aligner citation, removes the explicit closest-work comparison with MOD, and deletes the supplementary pluralism/fairness discussion and associated distinct references. The main positioning within personalized and decoding-time alignment remains.

P1.justification: PRM is renamed PersRM, related work is condensed, computational-cost prose is revised, and acknowledgments are added. The appendices are reorganized and limitations relocated, while most of the main narrative remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Localized display changes include configuration rows in Table 2, reordered metric columns and removal of the weight column in Table 3, revised Figure 5 axes, and a memory column in Table C2. Algorithms are added, while Table B2 and Figure B1 are removed. The overall visual design remains similar.

improvement.justification: Pseudocode, explicit single/joint comparisons, memory accounting, and revised Table 3 aggregates improve clarity. However, Section 4.2 still describes joint alignment while highlighting single-dimension results; training coverage conflicts with the retained UltraFeedback preprocessing text, and model-specific beta settings are lost. These issues directly affect interpretation and reproducibility, so the benefits and harms do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
